subtitle: Shivaji’s March to the Southern Horizon

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of an army on the move across the Deccan plateau
panels.action: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj rides at the head of a long Maratha column crossing a dry plateau toward distant southern forts, banners snapping in the wind under a vast sky.

dialogue.text: In 1677, Shivaji, Hindu king of the west, joined hands with Abu Hasan, Muslim sultan of Golconda, and marched south—not for faith, but for the future of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: १६७७ में शिवाजी, पश्चिम के हिंदू राजा, ने गोलकुंडा के मुस्लिम सुल्तान अबू हसन से हाथ मिलाया और दक्षिण कूच किया—धर्म नहीं, दक्खन के भविष्य के लिए।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Shivaji over a campaign map lit by oil lamps
panels.action: Inside a stone hall, Shivaji leans over a large cloth map showing the Deccan and far Karnataka, pins marking forts like Vellore and Gingee, as aides stand respectfully in the gloom.

dialogue.text: By the late 1670s, the Mughal tide pressed from the north, Bijapur still watched from the east, and Shivaji’s gaze turned beyond the Ghats to the rich plains of Karnataka.

i18n.hi: १६७० के दशक के अंत तक उत्तर से मुगल लहर चढ़ रही थी, पूरब में बीजापुर घूर रहा था, और शिवाजी की नज़र घाटों के पार कर्नाटक के समृद्ध मैदानी इलाकों पर जा टिकी।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Shivaji’s thoughtful face, profile lit against darkness
panels.action: Shivaji stands by an open jharokha at night, the faint lights of a Deccan town below, his face lined with care as he grips the hilt of his sword loosely.

dialogue.text: There, south of the Tungabhadra, lay old jagirs of Shahaji, his father; there too lay the line of Venkoji, his half-brother, and the shadow of Bijapur’s broken but lingering power.

i18n.hi: तूंगभद्रा के दक्षिण में शाहाजी, उनके पिता की पुरानी जागीरें थीं; वहीं वेणकोजी, सौतेले भाई की रियासत और बीजापुर की टूटी पर बाकी ताकत की छाया भी।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of the Deccan showing three powers in different colors
panels.action: A stylized map-view shows regions tinted for Golconda, Bijapur and Maratha domains, with arrows of Mughal advance pushing down and new routes sketched toward the southeast.

dialogue.text: To stand against the Mughal-Bijapur squeeze, Shivaji needed depth—new strongholds, fresh revenues, allies who feared imperial overreach as much as he did.

i18n.hi: मुगल‑बीजापुर की जकड़ से निपटने को शिवाजी को गहराई चाहिए थी—नए गढ़, ताज़ी आमदनी, और ऐसे साथी जो बादशाही हद से उतने ही डरते हों जितना वह।

panels.shot: courtly mid-shot of Shivaji dictating a letter to a scribe
panels.action: Seated cross-legged on a carpet, Shivaji speaks calmly while a court scribe bends over palm-leaf and paper, capturing his words that will ride east toward Hyderabad.

dialogue.text: So letters rode out from Raigad to Hyderabad, to Abu Hasan Qutb Shah of Golconda—a Persianate court, Shia Muslim, but a Deccani kingdom wary of Aurangzeb’s hunger.

i18n.hi: तो रायगढ़ से हैदराबाद तक खत उड़ चले—गोलकुंडा के कुतुबशाह अबू हसन के नाम; फ़ारसी रंग का दरबार, शिया हुकूमत, पर औरंगज़ेब के लालच से चौकन्ना दक्खनी मुल्क।

panels.shot: opulent interior wide of the Golconda court
panels.action: In a richly decorated hall with stucco arches and carpets, Abu Hasan Qutb Shah sits on a low throne among courtiers as a messenger bows, presenting a letter sealed with Shivaji’s emblem.

dialogue.text: Golconda’s rulers had long balanced Mughal threats with alliances. An offer from a rising Maratha king promised a new axis of defense across the Deccan.

i18n.hi: गोलकुंडा के शासक हमेशा मुगल ख़तरे और दोस्तियों के बीच संतुलन साधते आए थे। उभरते मराठा राजा की पेशकश ने दक्खन में बचाव की नई धुरी का वादा किया।

panels.shot: medium shot on Abu Hasan in deliberation with advisors
panels.action: Abu Hasan Qutb Shah, bearded and richly robed, gestures thoughtfully with his hand as Deccani and foreign courtiers lean in, some cautious, some eager, in the candlelit hall.

dialogue.text: Abu Hasan weighed the risks; but the Mughals menaced his northern frontiers, and Bijapur’s decline stirred old ambitions. A pact with Shivaji could carve a shared buffer in the south.

i18n.hi: अबू हसन ने जोखिम तौले; मगर मुगल उसकी उत्तरी सरहदों पर दबाव थे, और बीजापुर की गिरावट ने पुरानी तमन्नाएँ जगा दीं। शिवाजी से गठबंधन दक्षिण में साझा बफर गढ़ सकता था।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of a field camp where envoys meet
panels.action: On open ground between tents, Shivaji stands with a dignified emissary of Golconda; behind them rise the banners of both states and the distant walls of a Deccan fort.

dialogue.text: The alliance that followed was practical and clear: Golconda subsidies and passage, Maratha arms in the field, shared gains in the Karnataka where Bijapur and local chiefs still held sway.

i18n.hi: जो समझौता हुआ वो साफ और ठोस था—गोलकुंडा से रुपया और रास्ता, मैदान में मराठा की तलवार, और कर्नाटक में साझा हिस्सा, जहाँ बीजापुर और देसी सरदारों का अभी भी दबदबा था।

panels.shot: wide tracking shot of the Maratha army entering Golconda-held territory
panels.action: Shivaji rides through a broad valley, his cavalry stretching behind him as Deccani officials watch from the roadside, some curious, some wary, under the gaze of distant hills.

dialogue.text: English factors from distant Madras recorded the march with cold curiosity: a western Hindu king moving under a Muslim sultan’s sanction, toward the Tamil and Kannada lands.

i18n.hi: दूर के मद्रास से अंग्रेज फैक्टरों ने इस कूच को ठंडी नज़र से लिखा—पश्चिम का हिंदू राजा, मुस्लिम सुल्तान की इजाज़त में, तमिल और कन्नड़ इलाकों की ओर बढ़ता।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of Maratha troops crossing a river
panels.action: Shivaji’s soldiers wade and ferry across a broad river with pack-bullocks and cannon, officers directing men toward a rising escarpment dotted with unknown forts.

dialogue.text: This was not a raid but a campaign. Grain trains, siege guns, locally hired guides and interpreters moved with the host, knitting Maharashtra to the far south with dusty roads and shared danger.

i18n.hi: ये लूट नहीं, मुहिम थी। अनाज के काफिले, घेराबंदी की तोपें, इसी ज़मीन के गाइड और दुभाषिए फौज के साथ चले, धूल भरी राहों पर महाराष्ट्र को दूर दक्षिण से जोड़ते हुए।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Vellore fort in the distance
panels.action: Massive stone walls and high bastions of Vellore rise ahead, palm trees swaying nearby, as Shivaji and his captains halt on a ridge to survey the formidable fortress.

dialogue.text: Targets were chosen with care. Forts like Vellore controlled passes, trade and armies. Each stronghold taken would be a knot binding Maratha influence to the southern plains.

i18n.hi: निशाने सोचे‑समझे थे। वेल्लोर जैसे किले दरें, कारोबार और फौजों पर काबू रखते। हर जीता गढ़ मराठा असर को दक्षिणी मैदानों से बाँधने वाली एक गाँठ था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji consulting a local ally outside Vellore
panels.action: In a grove near the fort, Shivaji listens intently to a local nayak or intermediary, who points toward Vellore’s walls, while Maratha officers stand ready behind them.

dialogue.text: Here, too, statecraft moved ahead of steel. Some commanders bargained, some defected, some weighed which side would better guard their income and their shrines.

i18n.hi: यहाँ भी तलवार से पहले दिमाग चला। कुछ सरदार सौदे पर झुके, कुछ ने पलटी मारी, कुछ ने तौला किस तरफ से उनकी आमदनी और देवस्थान ज़्यादा महफूज़ रहेंगे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Gingee fort looming over rugged hills
panels.action: The towering ramparts and hilltop citadel of Gingee dominate a rocky landscape, layers of walls and bastions extending across the ridges under a hot, hazy sky.

dialogue.text: Further east stood Gingee, its triple hills and deep defenses famed in the south. To control it was to command a citadel that could outlast storms of war.

i18n.hi: ज़रा आगे पूरब में जिंजी खड़ा था—तीन पहाड़ों पर, गहरी किलाबंदियाँ, पूरे दक्षिण में मशहूर। इसे पकड़ना यानी एक ऐसा गढ़ पाना जो युद्ध के तूफ़ान भी झेल सके।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Shivaji pointing toward Gingee with his sword
panels.action: From a vantage rock, Shivaji raises his sheathed sword and points toward Gingee’s heights while his officers watch, reading determination in his stance.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: A fort like this is a promise: for us, or against us.

i18n.hi: ऐसा किला एक वादा है—या हमारे लिए, या हमारे ख़िलाफ़।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Shivaji in a council tent
panels.action: Inside a large campaign tent, Shivaji sits with senior commanders, pointing to a rough sketch of forts and routes on the floor as they argue softly and weigh choices.

dialogue.text: Sabhasad later recounted the steady succession of sieges and submissions. Not every gate needed battering; some opened for timely payment, some for fear of future Mughal wrath.

i18n.hi: सभासद ने बाद में घेराबंदियों और सरेंडरों की ये निरंतर कड़ी लिखी। हर फाटक पर धावा ज़रूरी न था—कुछ रुपया देखकर खुले, कुछ मुगल के भावी कोप से डरकर।

panels.shot: wide of a local temple town with Maratha and local soldiers mingling
panels.action: In a busy temple town near a captured fort, Maratha soldiers share space with local troops and townsfolk, priests moving through the crowd, traders opening stalls warily.

dialogue.text: As forts fell, towns adjusted. Marathi commands and Kannada or Tamil tongues mingled in markets and shrines, as new garrisons promised order, tax collection and protection from distant emperors.

i18n.hi: किले झुके तो कस्बे बदले। मराठी हुक्म, कन्नड़‑तमिल ज़ुबानें, बाज़ारों और मंदिरों में घुली, नई छावनियों ने दूर बैठे बादशाहों से बचाव, टैक्स वसूली और अमन की गारंटी दी।

panels.shot: tense mid-shot of Shivaji receiving news about Mysore
panels.action: A breathless messenger kneels before Shivaji, who listens, brows knit, while another officer holds a rolled letter bearing the seal of a Mysore notable.

dialogue.text: Yet the land was not empty. Mysore’s Wodeyar ruler and other chiefs watched this new power from the west. Some resisted, some bargained, judging whether Maratha rule would be lighter than old overlords.

i18n.hi: पर ज़मीन खाली न थी। मैसूर के वोडियर शासक और दूसरे नायक पश्चिम से उठती इस नई ताकत को देखते रहे। कुछ भिड़े, कुछ ने सौदे किए, तौलते हुए कि मराठा राज पुराने मालिकों से हल्का पड़ेगा या नहीं।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot of Shivaji reading a letter by lamplight
panels.action: At night in his tent, Shivaji reads a letter with Shahaji’s name mentioned, his expression softening for a moment as memories of his father’s southern years flicker in his eyes.

dialogue.text: For Shivaji, Karnataka was not foreign soil. His father Shahaji had served and held jagirs here under Bijapur. To him, this march also reclaimed a family claim and secured distant kin.

i18n.hi: शिवाजी के लिए कर्नाटक पराई धरती न थी। पिता शाहाजी ने यहीं बीजापुर के अधीन नोकरी की, जागीरें लीं। ये कूच उनके लिए बाप की मिल्कियत लौटाना और दूर के कुनबे को साधना भी था।

panels.shot: dramatic two-shot of Shivaji confronting Venkoji in a hall
panels.action: In a high-pillared southern hall, Shivaji faces his half-brother Venkoji, who stands in rich court dress, arms folded, while attendants and guards stand tense in the background.

dialogue.text: Most delicate of all was Venkoji of Thanjavur, Shahaji’s younger son. Between them lay shared blood, old rights in the south, and the question of who would rule which lands.

i18n.hi: सबसे नाज़ुक मामला था तंजावूर के वेणकोजी का, शाहाजी का छोटा बेटा। बीच में साझा खून, दक्षिण की पुरानी रियासतें, और सवाल—किसका हुक्म किस ज़मीन पर चले।

panels.shot: medium close-up alternating between Shivaji and Venkoji
panels.action: A split composition shows Shivaji calm but firm, and Venkoji proud yet uneasy, each weighing words before they speak in the hushed hall.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: Let our father’s house not weaken itself while others circle these lands.

i18n.hi: चलो, हमारे बाप का घर खुद को कमज़ोर न करे, जब दूसरे इन इलाकों पर नज़र गड़ाए घूम रहे हों।

panels.shot: wide shot of scribes and officials drafting a settlement
panels.action: Scribes sit in a row on the floor, writing on long sheets as officials from both sides point out clauses, while outside the window palm trees and the river plain stretch away.

dialogue.text: Through days of talk came settlement: obligations for Venkoji to pay, territories to acknowledge, a recognition that Shivaji’s sway now reached into the Thanjavur orbit, though Venkoji kept his throne.

i18n.hi: कई दिन की बात‑चीत के बाद समझौता तय हुआ—वेणकोजी पर अदायगी की शर्तें, मान ली गई ज़मीनें, और ये मान्यता कि शिवाजी का असर अब तंजावूर तक जा पहुँचता है, भले गद्दी वेणकोजी के हाथ रही।

panels.shot: wide of the coastline near Madras with distant European ships
panels.action: On a hazy coastline, small Indian craft move near the shore while far off, towering European sailing ships anchor, their flags barely visible, as smoke curls up from a fort like Madras.

dialogue.text: From Madras, English factors wrote of these shifts with unease. New powers in Vellore and Gingee could threaten trade routes, or be bargained with against rivals.

i18n.hi: मद्रास से अंग्रेज फैक्टर इन बदले हालात पर घबराहट से लिखते रहे। वेल्लोर और जिंजी में नई ताकतें समंदर पार कारोबार को काट भी सकती थीं, या दुश्मनों के ख़िलाफ़ नए सौदे भी दिला सकती थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji in prayer or quiet reflection before departure
panels.action: Within a small shrine near a captured fort, Shivaji stands with folded hands before a simple deity, his sword resting against the wall, as the murmurs of his camp drift in from outside.

dialogue.text: By year’s end, a chain of forts, revenues and understandings tied Maharashtra to the south. Shivaji had not planted a new capital here, but he had planted options.

i18n.hi: साल के अंत तक किलों, आमदनियों और समझौतों की एक ज़ंजीर ने महाराष्ट्र को दक्षिण से जोड़ दिया। शिवाजी ने यहाँ नया राजधानी नहीं बसाई, पर नई राहों की पौध ज़रूर लगा दी।

panels.shot: heroic low-angle wide of Shivaji’s army beginning its return north
panels.action: Shivaji, slightly older and more weathered, turns his horse northward as his banners swing around; behind him, the walls of a southern fort stand under the watch of a newly left garrison.

dialogue.text: Later, Rajaram would use Gingee as a refuge against Mughal storms. That future was possible because this campaign had laid foundations far beyond the Sahyadris.

i18n.hi: बाद में राजाराम ने जिंजी को मुगल तूफ़ानों से बचने का सहारा बनाया। वो मसरूफ भविष्य इस मुहिम की रखी हुई नींव पर ही खड़ा हो सका, जो सह्याद्रि से बहुत आगे डली थी।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Shivaji’s steady eyes, fading into maps and flags
panels.action: Shivaji’s eyes fill the frame, calm and resolved, as faint overlays of maps, forts, and both Maratha and Golconda flags fade in the background like memories of choices made.

dialogue.text: In an age later sliced into religious lines, this march tells another truth: Shivaji chose allies and foes by power and purpose, not by creed—a lesson in politics that still unsettles easy tales.

i18n.hi: एक ज़माना जिसे बाद में धर्म की लकीरों से काटकर बताया गया, उसमें ये कूच दूसरी सच्चाई दिखाता है—शिवाजी ने दोस्त‑दुश्मन ताकत और मकसद से चुने, मज़हब से नहीं; सियासत का ऐसा सबक जो आज भी आसान कहानियों को हिला देता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Shivaji’s March to the Southern Horizon
subtitle_i18n.hi: शिवाजी की दक्षिण की ओर चढ़ाई
